data.content_ref: inline:SRC_03 attributes resilience to 'operational heterogeneity' of the decentralized network but its own countercondition (monolith with N-version programming) admits the monolith can achieve the same heterogeneity internally. The leap-second 'stochastic filter' mechanism depends only on implementation diversity, not on who operates the service, so it cannot causally distinguish the decentralized network from a large service with N-version internal redundancy. Since the problem requires arguing for/against the decentralized network vs. a strictly-more-redundant large service, an attack surface where the monolith can match the heterogeneity undermines the claimed resilience advantage.
